B2AI_ORG:114.title: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project

data.name: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
data.title: Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project
data.description: The AI-READI flagship dataset is a multimodal, AI-ready dataset collected from 2,280 adults aged 40 and older with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), harmonized across three United States data collection sites (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, and University of Washington). Version 3.0.0 contains data collected between 19 July 2023 and 1 May 2025 spanning survey data, clinical data mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model, 12-lead electrocardiography in WFDB, retinal photography, optical coherence tomography, optical coherence tomography angiography and fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy in DICOM, home environmental sensing, continuous glucose monitoring and wearable activity monitoring. Recruitment sampling aimed at an approximately equal distribution of participants across race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes severity (no diabetes; pre-diabetes or lifestyle-controlled; oral or non-insulin-injectable medication controlled; insulin controlled) so that downstream AI/ML analyses are feasible in ways they are not with claims or electronic health record data. The stated goal is to better understand salutogenesis, the pathway from disease to health, in T2DM. This public version contains no protected health information; information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of participants and medications used has also been removed and is held in a controlled-access version obtainable under a data use agreement.
data.was_derived_from: AI Ready and Exploratory Atlas for Diabetes Insights (AI-READI) observational study
data.conforms_to: Organized following the Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1: one directory per datatype at the root, then one folder per modality, then one folder per device, then one folder per participant named after the participant's study ID number. Per-datatype file format standards are the WaveForm DataBase (WFDB) for cardiac_ecg; the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model for clinical_data, where each CSV file is a one-to-one mapping to an OMOP CDM table; the NASA ASCII File Format Guidelines for Earth Science Data for environment; Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) for retinal_flio, retinal_oct, retinal_octa and retinal_photography; and Open mHealth for wearable_activity_monitor and wearable_blood_glucose. A separate RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT metadata package conforming to the FAIRSCAPE profile 0.1 describes the 3.0.0 release and its nine sub-crates.

purposes.response: To enable future generations of artificial intelligence and machine learning research to provide critical insights into type 2 diabetes mellitus, including salutogenic pathways to return to health.

To permit downstream pseudotime manifold analysis, an approach used to predict disease trajectories by collecting and learning from complex, multimodal data from participants with differing disease severity, and so to reconstruct a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal towards health.

To establish standards, best practices and guidelines for the collection, preparation and sharing of data for AI/ML purposes, and to serve as a model and blueprint for future data generation projects, following the Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable principles.

addressing_gaps.response: The lack of well-designed, high quality, large and inclusive multimodal datasets that are AI ready for training AI models on complex, multi-organ diseases such as T2DM.

The under-representation in past research of racial and ethnic groups that bear a higher burden of disease; a meta-epidemiological review of T2DM studies published from 2000 to 2020 found that samples lacked racial and ethnic diversity.
The infeasibility of downstream AI/ML analyses with existing data sources such as claims or electronic health records data, which the multi-domain acquisition protocol is designed to overcome.

tasks.response: Pseudotime manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories from complex, multimodal data across participants of differing disease severity, from normal to insulin-dependent T2DM.
Development of AI/ML models on a hypothesis-agnostic, multimodal T2DM dataset, using the recommended 70/15/15 training, validation and testing split distributed with the release.

instances.instance_type: An individual patient. Each instance consists of all of the data available for one individual participating in the study, across survey, clinical, retinal imaging, environmental sensor, continuous glucose monitor and wearable activity monitor modalities.
instances.label_description: No labels or targets are provided. The healthsheet records that no specific labeling was performed, as the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic and aimed at facilitating multiple potential downstream AI/ML applications, and that no software was used to label instances.

missing: One or more data modalities for some participants
why_missing: Some participants elected not to participate in some study elements; in a few cases the data collection device had no stored results or was returned too late to retrieve the results, for example because the battery died or data were lost; in a few cases a data collision occurred at some point in the process and data were lost.

instances.notes: The modalities encompass tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data; there is no unstructured text data in the dataset. The first version of the dataset contained 204 instances and the second 1,067 instances.

relationships.relationship_details: All instances are part of the same prospective data generation project (AI-READI). There is currently only one visit per participant, so instances are not linked longitudinally in this version.

splits.split_details: The release includes a recommended split into training, validation and testing sets in 70%/15%/15% proportions, distributed in the participants.tsv metadata file. Because sex, race and ethnicity are not released with the public version of the dataset, the project team prepared the split so that the validation and test sets are balanced as well as possible for sex, race/ethnicity and diabetes status (no diabetes; pre-diabetes or lifestyle controlled; oral medication controlled; insulin controlled). The split totals 1,576 training, 352 validation and 352 test participants, with a mean age of 60.8 +/- 11.3 years overall. The split is new in version 3.0.0 and is described as aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using this dataset.

subpopulations.identification: Self-reported race and ethnicity in four groups (Asian, Black, Hispanic, White), used to triple-balance recruitment and to balance the recommended validation and test splits.
subpopulations.distribution: Across all 2,280 participants: Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, White 836. The study population statement records an aim of recruiting 1,000 subjects from each of the four groups.
subpopulations.notes: Race and ethnicity variables are not released with the public version of the dataset and are held under controlled access; the healthsheet answers "No" to whether the dataset identifies demographic sub-populations. Only the aggregate counts published in the README are available publicly.

subpopulations.identification: Biological sex, used to triple-balance recruitment and the recommended splits.
subpopulations.notes: Sex is not released with the public version of the dataset and is held under controlled access.

subpopulations.identification: Diabetes severity group in four categories: no diabetes; pre-diabetes or Type 2 diabetes controlled by lifestyle adjustments; Type 2 diabetes controlled by oral or non-insulin injectable medications; Type 2 diabetes controlled by insulin.
subpopulations.distribution: Across all 2,280 participants: no diabetes 776, lifestyle 560, oral 686, insulin 258. The study protocol aimed to recruit approximately 1,000 patients into each of the four groups.
subpopulations.notes: Unlike sex and race/ethnicity, diabetes status is released with the public version: the healthsheet states only that "sex, race, and ethnicity data are not being released with the public version of the dataset", and the README split table reports diabetes status counts for the training, validation and test sets publicly.

anomalies.anomaly_details: In survey data, skipped questions or incomplete responses are expected.

In wearable data, improper use and technical failure such as battery failure or system malfunction are expected. The Garmin activity monitor has gaps in data collection because the battery had to be charged every two to three days.
In imaging data, patient uncooperation, noise that may obscure the images, technical failure such as system malfunction, and data transfer failures are expected.
In a few cases there may have been a data collision at some point in the process, resulting in lost data.

Image quality for the undilated handheld Optomed Aurora fundus camera varies from patient to patient and within the same patient, because obtaining a good view is challenging without dilation and the device is handheld.

known_biases.bias_description: Participants are volunteers, so the sample is subject to volunteer bias, which may limit the generalizability of results to those not represented in the study population.

Recruitment is predominantly urban and hospital-based, which may not fully capture all possible cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds, and the cohort does not include other races and ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans.
known_biases.mitigation_strategy: Three recording sites were strategically selected for geographic variability across the United States and to ensure representation across various racial and ethnic groups, and individuals from all demographic backgrounds were recruited at all three sites.

known_biases.bias_description: Although the cross-sectional database ultimately aims to achieve balance across race/ethnicity, biological sex, and diabetes presence and severity, interim releases are not balanced across these parameters; as enrollment is ongoing, periodic updates to data releases may not have achieved balanced distribution across groups.
affected_subsets: The pilot data release and subsequent periodic version releases, including this one.
known_biases.mitigation_strategy: Uniform data collection protocols were implemented for all subjects irrespective of race/ethnicity, biological sex, or diabetes severity, across all study sites, and the study sites were selected to ensure varied representation and minimize the potential for sampling bias.

known_biases.bias_description: Eligibility required participants to speak and read English, which the protocol publication notes may have created challenges in recruiting Hispanic and/or Asian persons.

known_limitations.limitation_description: The study cohort may not provide a comprehensive representation of the population: recruitment is predominantly urban and hospital-based and the cohort excludes races and ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans.
known_limitations.scope_impact: Limits the generalization of models derived from the dataset to populations outside the three recruiting health systems and the four represented racial/ethnic groups.

known_limitations.limitation_description: Not all modalities are available for all participants, because of non-participation in some study elements, device failure, late device return or data loss.

The public version withholds information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of participants and medications used, and holds 5-digit zip code, genetic sequencing data, past health records, medications, and traffic and accident reports under controlled access.
known_limitations.recommended_mitigation: The full dataset is accessible by entering into a data use agreement.

known_limitations.limitation_description: The study is cross-sectional and there is currently only one visit per participant, so the dataset does not support within-participant longitudinal analysis in this version.
Eligibility restricted enrollment to adults aged 40 to 85 who could read and speak English and provide consent, and excluded pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes.

content_warnings.notes: The healthsheet answers "No" to whether the dataset contains data that, if viewed directly, might be offensive, insulting, threatening, or might otherwise pose any safety risk such as psychological safety and anxiety.

confidential_elements.confidentiality_details: The healthsheet records that the dataset does not contain data that might be considered confidential and that no personally identifiable information is included in the dataset. The RO-Crate records a confidentiality level of "HL7:2N (normal)".

sensitive_elements.sensitivity_details: The public dataset does not contain data considered sensitive; the released data contain no protected health information, and information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of the participants as well as medications used has been removed. The sensitive variables collected by the study - racial and ethnic origins, 5-digit zip code, motor vehicle accident reports, genetic sequencing data, past health records and medications - are withheld from this release and held in the separate controlled-access version.

is_deidentified.method: No active de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected; the team checked that no identifiable data per US HIPAA were present. The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule via the "Safe Harbor" method.
is_deidentified.identifiers_removed: Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule (Safe Harbor method); Information related to the sex of participants; Information related to the race and ethnicity of participants; Medications used
is_deidentified.deidentification_details: The FAIRhub de-identification level is recorded as deIdentType "NoDeIdentification" with deIdentDirect true and deIdentHIPAA true, and dates, non-arrayed values and k-anonymity flags false. Sex and race/ethnicity were removed from the public set to prevent stigmatization of findings. The RO-Crate records the release as deidentified.
is_deidentified.notes: A theoretical risk of future re-identification is acknowledged: AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification. To prevent re-identification attempts the project implements a robust data dissemination system, a strict license agreement and data watermarking for both public and controlled sets; the license states that the Data may be statically watermarked to identify the Licensee.

special_protections: Eligibility excluded pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes, and set a minimum age of 40 years and a maximum of 85 years, so no minors were enrolled. The IRB protocol records that the research will not recruit or obtain data from individuals known to be prisoners, is not likely to have subjects who become prisoners while participating, does not purposefully include fetuses, neonates or pregnant women, and does not include cognitively impaired adults or other adults unable to consent. Native American or non-U.S. indigenous populations are not actively recruited through a tribe or tribe-focused organization.
at_risk_populations.notes: Separately from this dataset, the funded project committed to engaging in a tribal consultation to address barriers and facilitators of participation, with the goal of collecting similar data within a Native American cohort in an ethical and respectful manner, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes engagement with the Native Biodata Consortium as a co-learning opportunity. These are stated as project activities, not as content of this release.

irb_approval: University of Washington IRB protocol STUDY00016228, with initial approval received on 20 December 2022 and an annual renewal application required within 90 days of expiration. Reliance agreements were in place with the IRBs of the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego, which used the same consent form with minor institution-specific language.
human_subject_research.ethics_review_board: The RO-Crate names the reviewing body as "Washington University IRB" with the contact given as the IRB Reliance Team, hsdrely@uw.edu, at the Human Subjects Division, University of Washington, 4333 Brooklyn Ave NE Box 359470, Seattle, WA 98195-9470, US. The FAIRhub study description records the human subject review status as "Submitted, approved".
regulatory_compliance: The study is recorded as not FDA-regulated for drugs or for devices, and as having no data monitoring committee. Written informed consent was provided by all participants. Licensees must comply with NIH data security and privacy standards under the Genomic Data Sharing Policy.
special_populations: Adults aged 40 to 85 years, with and without type 2 diabetes
Pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes were exclusion criteria
No children, prisoners or adults unable to consent were enrolled

ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization: University of Washington Institutional Review Board
ethical_reviews.review_details: Protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 20 December 2022, with reliance agreements covering the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego sites; an annual renewal application about the status and progress of the study is required within 90 days of expiration. The initial approval letter is published with the dataset documentation.
ethical_reviews.source_caveats: The RO-Crate labels the reviewing organization "Washington University IRB" while giving the University of Washington Human Subjects Division as its address and hsdrely@uw.edu as its contact; the protocol publication and the healthsheet both place the approving IRB at the University of Washington.

ethical_reviews.review_details: The RO-Crate records ethical review by four named individuals - Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans - without naming an organization or committee. The project states that ethical, legal and social implications are considered at every stage of the project cycle and that guidance from bioethicists informs the standards, best practices and guidelines for collection, preparation and sharing of the data.
ethical_reviews.source_caveats: No reviewing organization is recorded because the bundle attaches no body name to these four reviewers; the RO-Crate ethicalReview field lists only the individuals.

ethical_reviews.review_details: A Community Advisory Board of 11 persons from the three sites, including diversity in race and ethnicity as represented in the AI-READI sample, contributes to the development of the protocol; the IRB protocol records that the board evaluates the consent forms and research protocols and that its feedback is considered in modifications.

informed_consent.consent_type: Written informed consent, obtained either electronically before the visit (e-consent with an electronic signature through REDCap) or in person at the start of the visit for participants who did not select the electronic option.
informed_consent.consent_documentation: The approved consent form for the principal project site, the University of Washington, is published with the dataset documentation; the other clinical sites had IRB reliance and used the same consent form with minor institution-specific language incorporated according to individual institutional requirements. Upon signing, the signed consent form was automatically emailed to the subject, and additional copies could be requested from the study coordinator for the duration of the study.
informed_consent.consent_scope: The FAIRhub consent metadata records the consent type as "ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised" with no non-commercial, geographic, research-type, genetic-only or methods restrictions flagged, and notes that the public version of the dataset can only be used for type 2 diabetes related research while a private version allows more generic use. Consent was required before participation in any part of the protocol, including questionnaires.
informed_consent.withdrawal_mechanism: Participants were permitted to withdraw consent at any time and cease study participation.

collection_consents.consent_details: Potential participants were given the option to read all consent documentation electronically before their visit and to give consent with an electronic signature without verbal communication with a clinical research coordinator. Participants could access the e-consent documentation in REDCap and decide at that point not to participate or to request additional information, a call back or a video conference with study staff. No study-specific questionnaires other than the screening questionnaire were available until consent had been given.

consent_revocations.revocation_details: Any data that had been shared or used up to the point of withdrawal would stay in the dataset; this is clearly communicated in the consent document. The IRB protocol records that subjects will not be able to withdraw their data or specimens from banking, secondary use or sharing.

collection_notifications.notification_details: Each individual was aware of the data collection, as this was active data collection directly from participants rather than passive collection or secondary use of existing data. Individuals identified from electronic health record screening were mailed a hardcopy invitation letter and sent an invitation email, both personalized to direct them into an online REDCap recruitment interface using links, access codes and QR codes, where they could read an overview of the research program, expectations for participation and answers to frequently asked questions.

collection_timeframes.timeframe_details: The DataCite "Collected" date recorded for this version is the range 2023-07-19/2025-05-01, described as the period when the data was collected; the healthsheet and README repeat this range for the 2,280 participants in version 3.0.0. The overall project timeline spans four years, with one year for protocol development and training and years two to four for subject recruitment and data collection; preliminary pilot enrollment ran from 18 July 2023 to 30 November 2023 and formal data collection began on 1 December 2023. The study start date is recorded as 2023-07-19 (actual) with an anticipated completion date of 2027-01-01.
collection_timeframes.source_caveats: The protocol publication states that enrollment began on 18 July 2023, one day earlier than the 2023-07-19 study start and collection-period start recorded in the higher-ranked FAIRhub metadata; the FAIRhub value is used here.

acquisition_methods.acquisition_details: Some data were directly observable, such as laboratory results, vital signs and retinal imaging. Verification of data entry was performed when possible, for example by cross-referencing entered medications with medications that were physically brought in or photographed by each study participant.

Other data were reported by subjects, notably survey and questionnaire responses covering demographics, depressive symptoms, diabetes distress and self-care, diet, smoking, alcohol, vaping and marijuana use, general health, social determinants of health, and visual impairment and eye care access.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: REDCap was used to collect patient-reported questionnaire data and clinical data recorded at the visit, including the medications assessment, vitals, visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, monofilament test results and complete blood count results. Clinical data outside expected minimum/maximum ranges were flagged in REDCap and appeared in reports viewed by clinical research coordinators and data managers. The exact forms used for data collection in REDCap are published with the dataset documentation.

Philips PageWriter TC30 Cardiograph (Amsterdam, The Netherlands): a 12-lead ECG performed while the participant sits in a reclining chair or lies supine, with the position recorded as 0, 30, 60 or 90 degrees relative to supine. Data are exported in .xml format and distributed under the WFDB standard in cardiac_ecg/ecg_12lead/philips_tc30.

LeeLab Anura environmental sensor, custom designed at the Karalis Johnson Retina Center, University of Washington (Seattle, Washington). Participants were sent home with the device and asked to place it in a frequently used area of the home for 10 continuous days, then to note where it had been placed. It records ambient temperature, relative humidity, nitrogen oxides (NO and NO2), volatile organic compounds, particulate matter counts (PM1.0, PM2.5, PM4 and PM10) and 11 multi-spectral light intensity measurements, exported as .csv.
collection_mechanisms.notes: The device was specifically chosen with participant privacy as a primary concern: it does not capture video or audio, is not equipped with GPS location monitoring and is not synced with participant-owned devices.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Dexcom G6 Continuous Glucose Monitor (Dexcom, Inc., San Diego, California): a real-time integrated continuous glucose monitoring system worn continuously for 10 days that captures blood glucose readings in mg/dL every five minutes without finger sticks. A single sensor is designed to last a maximum of ten days and the transmitter saves data for thirty days, so data must be downloaded within that window. Participants were masked to the results during the monitoring period.
collection_mechanisms.notes: Dexcom provided research discounts on study devices. The IRB protocol additionally permits participants already wearing a Dexcom G6 either to place an additional study sensor or to share their existing Dexcom Clarity data, and offers them the option of allowing download of previously collected glucose values for up to 90 days before the visit, for a total of up to 100 days; the dataset documentation describes the collected CGM data as a 10-day monitoring period.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Garmin Vivosmart 5 physical activity monitor (Garmin Ltd, Schaffhausen, Switzerland). Advised to be worn on the non-dominant wrist for 10 consecutive days, with participants free to choose their preferred wrist, and returned with a form specifying the wrist worn and the dominant hand. The sampling frequency is 5 seconds and the device continuously records physical activity and sleep, including number of steps, heart rate, sleep duration, oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, stress and calories. Data are exported in .FIT format and converted to the Open mHealth standard.
collection_mechanisms.notes: There are gaps in data collection because the battery had to be charged every two to three days. Garmin provided research discounts on study devices. Like the environmental sensor, the tracker was chosen for privacy: it captures no video or audio, has no GPS location monitoring and is not synced with participant-owned devices.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Optomed Aurora IQ handheld fundus camera (Optomed, Oulu, Finland): a non-mydriatic camera with a 50-degree field of view, 5 Mpix sensor and high-contrast optical design, used to take undilated macula- and disc-centered color fundus photographs in a dark room with the participant seated and reclined. Output is DICOM.
collection_mechanisms.notes: Optomed loaned devices for research purposes at no cost.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: iCare EIDON widefield TrueColor confocal fundus imaging system (iCare USA, Inc., Raleigh, North Carolina): captures images up to 200 degrees with TrueColor, blue, red, red-free and infrared confocal modalities, operating without dilation at a minimum pupil of 2.5 mm. AI-READI images comprise single field central infrared/fundus autofluorescence and a smart horizontal mosaic, acquired in fully automated mode in a dark room to minimize operator-induced noise. Output is DICOM.
collection_mechanisms.notes: iCare World loaned devices for research purposes at no cost.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Heidelberg Spectralis HRA optical coherence tomography and OCT angiography system (Heidelberg Engineering GmbH, Heidelberg, Germany): combines OCT with retinal angiography using confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscope technology that minimizes the effects of light scatter. AI-READI scans are optic nerve head radial circle high resolution, posterior pole macula high resolution 61 lines, and macula 20x20 high speed 512 lines OCTA, acquired in a dark room. Output is DICOM.
collection_mechanisms.notes: Heidelberg Engineering provided research discounts on study devices.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Heidelberg Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Ophthalmoscopy (FLIO) (Heidelberg Engineering GmbH, Heidelberg, Germany): a macula-centered, non-invasive measurement of the fluorescence lifetimes of endogenous retinal fluorophores, recorded at short (498-560 nm) and long (560-720 nm) wavelengths and provided as two DICOM files per eye. Exported in .sdt file format and converted to DICOM for the dataset. Because the scan takes longer than a standard OCT and exposes participants to uncomfortable light levels, it is performed last in the visit.

Topcon Maestro2 3D OCT-1 (Topcon Healthcare, Itabashi-ku, Tokyo, Japan): a robotic OCT and color fundus camera capturing 12x9 mm wide-field OCT including macula and optic disc, 6x6 mm 3D macula OCT and 6x6 mm OCTA at a 50 kHz scan rate, acquired automatically in a dark room with minimal operator involvement. Exported in .fda file format and converted to DICOM for the dataset.
collection_mechanisms.notes: Topcon Corporation loaned devices for research purposes at no cost.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Topcon Triton DRI OCT (Topcon Healthcare, Itabashi-ku, Tokyo, Japan): swept-source OCT with a 1,050 nm wavelength light source and a non-mydriatic color fundus camera, visualizing the deepest layers of the eye including through cataracts. AI-READI protocols are 12x12 mm and 6x6 mm OCTA and 12.0x9.0x6.0 mm 3D horizontal and radial scans. Exported in .fda file format and converted to DICOM for the dataset.
collection_mechanisms.notes: Topcon Corporation loaned devices for research purposes at no cost.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Zeiss Cirrus 5000 Angioplex (Carl Zeiss Meditec AG, Jena, Germany): high-definition OCT with non-invasive imaging of retinal microvasculature. Protocols include 512x512 and 200x200 macula and optic nerve head cubes and 6x6 mm macula and disc OCTA, with a 60-degree OCTA widefield view, 8x8 mm single scans and 14x14 mm automated OCTA montage available. Output is DICOM.
collection_mechanisms.notes: Carl Zeiss loaned devices for research purposes at no cost.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: In-clinic measurement instruments whose readings were recorded into REDCap: the Montreal Cognitive Assessment administered on an iPad using the MoCA Duo application (MoCA Cognition, Quebec, Canada); the M&S Technologies Electronic Visual Acuity tester (Niles, Illinois) at 4 meters, with a 2.0 neutral density filter or ND-occluder for mesopic testing; the Mars letter contrast sensitivity chart (Mars Perceptrix, Chappaqua, New York) read monocularly under photopic and mesopic conditions with background luminance of 60 to 120 cd/m2; the Topcon KR-800 auto keratometer/refractor; a standard 10 g monofilament applied at three locations on each foot ten times per location with the participant's eyes closed; blood pressure by OMRON HEM 907XL, Medline MDS4001 or Welch Allyn 6000 series monitors, measured twice two minutes apart; and NIDEK LM-600P, Topcon CL-200 or Topcon CL-300 lensometers.

data_collectors.role: Clinical research coordinators and research assistants at the three sites
data_collectors.collector_details: Responsible for contacting and consenting research participants, ushering them through the research visit, conducting study visits including collection of ophthalmic images, training participants on study procedures such as continuous glucose monitoring and the fitness tracker, and ensuring the return of all study materials. All research personnel who recruited, enrolled and collected data underwent training by the data manager at the University of Alabama at Birmingham and worked from a detailed Manual of Procedures; a certification process was required of all coordinators, including mandatory institutional compliance training for human subject research and successful administration of all protocol elements to at least three volunteer practice subjects.
data_collectors.notes: Effort was supported by NIH award OT2OD032644 based on the percentage of effort contributed, with salaries aligned to the funding guidelines at each site.

data_collectors.collector_details: Data managers at each site oversaw the data collection process, reviewed REDCap range-check reports with the coordinators, ingested data into the REDCap database and extracted it for processing, and were responsible for the quality control of all data before uploading to FAIRhub.

The University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center testing facility performed the laboratory assays on stored frozen serum, plasma, whole blood and urine, returning results in .csv format.
Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments-certified laboratories local to each data collection site performed complete blood count testing on fresh whole blood samples.

direct_collection.collection_details: The data were collected directly from participants across the three recruiting sites. Recruitment pools were identified by screening electronic health records for diabetes and prediabetes ICD-10 codes for patients who had had an encounter with the sites' health systems. Some content of the dataset, such as past health records held under controlled access, derives from those electronic health records rather than from direct measurement.

sampling_strategies.strategies: Participants were recruited in waves to facilitate efficient sampling of the study base, with the composition and size of each wave influenced by the observed participation characteristics of race/ethnicity, gender, severity of T2DM and site; composition was monitored and adjusted by under- and oversampling groups as needed. For each wave a contact pool was identified by screening electronic health records at each site for ICD-10 diagnosis codes R73.09 and E11.X, with patients without diabetes identified as those without encounters with these codes. Recruitment aimed at approximately equal proportions of four race/ethnic groups, four categories of T2DM severity and biological males and females, rather than at matching the demographic distribution of the US population. The study is registered with a sampling method of "Non-Probability Sample" and an observational cohort, cross-sectional design.
sampling_strategies.source_data: All patients aged 40 years or older who had a medical encounter within each health system site (University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego, University of Washington) between 2020 and 2025.
sampling_strategies.why_not_representative: The cohort is deliberately balanced rather than demographically representative; recruitment is predominantly urban and hospital-based; participants are volunteers; and races and ethnicities such as Pacific Islanders and Native Americans are not included.
sampling_strategies.source_caveats: The bundle is internally inconsistent on whether the dataset is a sample. The healthsheet answers that "The dataset contains all possible instances", meaning all participants enrolled within the collection period, and answers "N/A" to the question of the sampling strategy used to draw the dataset from a larger set. Against this, the same-tier FAIRhub study description registers the samplingMethod as "Non-Probability Sample", and the protocol publication describes a defined study base (all patients aged 40 or older with an encounter at the three health systems between 2020 and 2025) from which wave-based, EHR-screened, balance-adjusted contact pools were drawn. `is_sample` is set true on the strength of the registered sampling method and the documented wave sampling; the healthsheet's "all possible instances" reading is best understood as a statement about completeness within the release window rather than about the relationship to the study base.

cleaning_strategies.cleaning_details: Quality control at the time of data entry and acquisition: clinical data outside expected minimum and maximum ranges were flagged in REDCap and visible in reports viewed by clinical research coordinators and data managers, who examined participant records and determined whether an error was likely. Data were checked, and edited where errors were detected, for credibility based on range checks, incorrect flow through prescribed skip patterns, missing data that could be directly filled from other portions of an individual's record, and the omission and/or duplication of records. Editing was done only under the guidance and approval of the site principal investigator; where there was no logical or appropriate way to correct the data, the site principal investigator reviewed the values and decided whether they should be removed.

The data manager at each data site was responsible for the quality control of all data before uploading to FAIRhub, and the dataset was reviewed internally by AI-READI team members for quality checks and to ensure that no personally identifiable information was accidentally included.

preprocessing_strategies.preprocessing_details: After data were sent from each study site to the central project team, all data were mapped to standardized terminologies where possible, notably the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model for observational clinical data and DICOM for medical imaging data, so that the dataset is stored and shared as "AI-ready" and enables immediate AI/ML research without reformatting and preprocessing.

Conversion of proprietary device exports into standard formats: Topcon Maestro2 and Triton data exported in .fda file format and converted to DICOM for the dataset; Heidelberg FLIO data exported in .sdt file format and converted to DICOM; Garmin activity data exported in .FIT file format and converted to the Open mHealth standard; ECG data converted to WFDB; environmental sensor and CGM exports handled as delimited text.

Removal of protected health information from the public release using the HIPAA Safe Harbor method, together with removal of information related to the sex and race/ethnicity of the participants and of medications used.

Organization of the release following the Clinical Dataset Structure v0.1.1, with a manifest.tsv metadata file in each datatype directory and root-level CDS metadata files including dataset_description.json, dataset_structure_description.json, study_description.json, participants.tsv, participants.json, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, healthsheet.md and LICENSE.txt. A dqd_omop.json file supports OMOP CDM data quality analysis with the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, which runs more than 3,500 data quality checks against an OMOP CDM instance.
Processing moved from custom and ad hoc handling for the v1.0.0 pilot data to a combination of automated and custom processing for the later data included in v2.0.0 and v3.0.0.

missing_data_documentation.missing_data_patterns: Not all modalities are available for all participants; Skipped questions and incomplete responses within survey data; Gaps within wearable activity monitor records
missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes: Some participants elected not to participate in some study elements; The data collection device did not have any stored results or was returned too late to retrieve the results, for example because the battery died or data were lost; A data collision at some point in the process, resulting in lost data; The Garmin activity monitor battery had to be charged every two to three days
missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy: Missing data that could be directly filled from other portions of an individual's record were filled during cleaning; otherwise values were left missing, or removed after review by the site principal investigator where no logical or appropriate correction was possible. No instances were excluded from the dataset at the time of preprocessing.

raw_data_sources.source_description: Study participants at the three data collection sites, who completed questionnaires, on-site measurements and imaging, and 10 days of at-home monitoring.
raw_data_sources.source_type: Direct prospective collection from human research participants

raw_data_sources.source_description: Electronic health records of the University of Alabama at Birmingham, University of California San Diego and University of Washington health systems, screened for eligibility and used to extract general health, eye health, medical and surgical history, diabetes, medications, laboratory records and prior imaging.
raw_data_sources.access_details: Past health records and medications derived from these sources are held under controlled access and are obtainable only by entering into a data use agreement; they are not part of the public release.

raw_sources.raw_data_details: Raw device and system exports before standardization: ECG in .xml, MoCA Duo application output (total score, section subscores, Memory Index Score and task completion times) in .csv, retinal images in device-native formats including Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt, Garmin activity data in .FIT, Dexcom CGM and environmental sensor data in .csv, laboratory results from the central laboratory in .csv, and REDCap exports. The raw data are saved and expected to be preserved by the AI-READI project at least for the duration of the project, but are not anticipated to be shared outside the project team at present, because they have not been mapped to standardized terminologies and because they may accidentally include personal health information or personally identifiable information, for example in free text fields. There is a possibility that raw data may be included in future releases of the controlled access dataset.

variables.derivation: Study identification number assigned to each enrolled participant.
variables.notes: Each participant folder in the dataset is named after the participant's ID number used in the study; the participants.tsv metadata file lists participants and their recommended split assignment.

variables.measurement_technique: Whole blood test performed by the University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center laboratory.
variables.notes: Included as a marker for diabetes; the testing laboratories provided a reference range of 4.0-6.0 %.

variables.measurement_technique: Serum test performed by the central laboratory on stored frozen samples.
variables.notes: Included as a marker for diabetes; the testing laboratories provided a reference range of 62-125 mg/dL. Blood was collected non-fasting.

variables.measurement_technique: EDTA plasma test performed by the central laboratory.
variables.notes: Included as an indicator of insulin production; reference range provided by the testing laboratories was 1.1-4.4 ng/mL.

variables.measurement_technique: Montreal Cognitive Assessment administered electronically on an iPad using the MoCA Duo application, capturing all participant responses interactively.
variables.notes: The total possible score is 30, with higher numbers representing better performance; a score below 24 is described as a sign of cognitive impairment and a final total score of 26 and above as normal. Section subscores, a Memory Index Score and task completion times are also exported. Scoring requires professional training and may be affected by education level, socioeconomic factors and depression or other mental health conditions.

variables.measurement_technique: M&S Technologies Electronic Visual Acuity tester at 4 meters, right and left eyes separately, under photopic conditions and under mesopic conditions through a 2.0 neutral density filter.
variables.notes: Expressed as the logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution, where lower numbers indicate better resolution. The Snellen visual acuity variables present in earlier versions were dropped in this version of the dataset, so only logMAR measurements are available.

variables.measurement_technique: Mars letter contrast sensitivity chart read monocularly under photopic conditions with a general occluder and under mesopic conditions with a neutral density occluder, in the standardized order photopic OD, photopic OS, mesopic OD, mesopic OS.
variables.notes: Expressed as log sensitivity, with higher numbers meaning better sensitivity. Testing was terminated when the patient made two consecutive errors or reached the end of the chart, and the log CS value was computed by multiplying the number of errors prior to the final correct letter by 0.04 and subtracting the result from the log CS value at the final correct letter.

variables.measurement_technique: Dexcom G6 continuous glucose monitor, one reading every five minutes.
variables.notes: Collected over a 10-day at-home monitoring period; participants were masked to the results during the monitoring period.

variables.measurement_technique: LeeLab Anura custom environmental sensor placed in the participant's home for 10 days.
variables.notes: Recorded alongside ambient temperature, relative humidity, nitrogen oxides (NO and NO2), volatile organic compounds and 11 multi-spectral light intensity measurements.

intended_uses.usage_notes: Data collection was specifically designed to permit downstream pseudotime manifold analysis, an approach used to predict disease trajectories by learning from complex, multimodal data from participants with differing disease severity, ranging from normal to insulin-dependent T2DM, with the long-term objective of reconstructing a temporal atlas of T2DM development and reversal towards health.

future_use_impacts.impact_details: A theoretical risk of future re-identification exists. AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification, so the project implements a robust data dissemination system, a strict license agreement and data watermarking for both public and controlled sets, and the license requires licensees who disseminate models trained on the Data to undertake all reasonable efforts to minimize the likelihood that Data can be memorized, derived, reconstructed or reconstituted through the use or construction of those models. Beyond this, the healthsheet states that the creators do not currently anticipate uses of the dataset that could result in unfair treatment or harm.

Because enrollment is ongoing and periodic releases may not have achieved balanced distribution across race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes severity, models developed on this version may reflect residual imbalance; future users should note that the balance targets apply to the completed cohort rather than to this interim release.

data.notes: The dataset description records an alternative title, "AI-READI dataset". A separate RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT metadata package conforming to the FAIRSCAPE profile 0.1 describes the 3.0.0 release and its nine sub-crates; it is a description of the dataset distributed outside the release itself, and does not appear among the nine root-level metadata files enumerated in the dataset structure description, so it is recorded in `conforms_to` prose rather than as a standard the dataset's own layout follows. Several negative findings recorded in the healthsheet are not carried by any structured slot: the dataset has not undergone any formal external audit, although it has been reviewed internally by AI-READI team members for quality checks and to ensure that no personally identifiable information was accidentally included; no data protection impact analysis has been conducted; the dataset had not been used for any tasks at the time of the release; there is no repository that links to papers or systems that use the dataset; there is currently no mechanism for others to extend or augment the AI-READI dataset outside those involved in the project; and there are no formal guidelines recommended to future researchers for creating new labels or defining new tasks. Beyond the NIH grants and Research to Prevent Blindness, the publications acknowledge in-kind support that is not grant funding: the Microsoft AI for Good Lab supported the cloud services needed for the project; Topcon Corporation, Optomed, iCare World and Carl Zeiss loaned devices for research purposes at no cost; and Heidelberg Engineering, Dexcom and Garmin provided research discounts on study devices. Biospecimens collected in the study - plasma, serum, buffy coats, genomic DNA, PAXgene RNA tubes and peripheral blood mononuclear cells - are banked at the University of Alabama at Birmingham Center for Clinical and Translational Science for future proteomics, metabolomics, genomics, gene expression and immunological studies, and are not part of this dataset; the protocol publication notes that the biorepository holds a finite number of samples and that procedures for reviewing and prioritizing written requests were still to be developed.
data.source_caveats: Publisher: two tier-1 sources disagree. The FAIRhub API records publisher.publisherName as "FAIRhub", while the RO-Crate records the publisher as "AI-READI Consortium". Because the sources share a tier the ranking cannot decide between them; the `publisher` slot carries the FAIRhub platform URI, and the RO-Crate's attribution of publication to the AI-READI Consortium is recorded here rather than silently discarded. Institutional attribution conflicts between tier-1 sources: the FAIRhub API records Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268) as managing organization, lead sponsor and affiliation of the principal investigator, and the license names it as Licensor, while the RO-Crate names the principal investigator as "Aaron Lee, Department of Ophthalmology, University of Washington" and labels the reviewing IRB "Washington University IRB" while giving the University of Washington Human Subjects Division address and hsdrely@uw.edu contact; NIH RePORTER (tier 4) and both publications (tier 3) place the award and the approving IRB at the University of Washington. Both attributions are represented rather than reconciled. Name expansion conflicts: the FAIRhub study description and NIH RePORTER expand AI-READI as "AI Ready and Exploratory Atlas for Diabetes Insights" and "Artificial Intelligence Ready and Exploratory Atlas for Diabetes Insights", while the protocol publication and the Nature Metabolism comment expand it as "Artificial Intelligence Ready and Equitable Atlas for Diabetes Insights"; the healthsheet uses the "Exploratory" form. Collection start date: the FAIRhub metadata gives 2023-07-19 as both the study start and the start of the collected-data range, while the protocol publication states that enrollment began on 18 July 2023; the tier-1 value is used. Target enrollment: the FAIRhub study description records an anticipated enrollment of 4,000 and the protocol publication and Nature comment give 4,000, while the IRB protocol (tier 2) states 4,600 across four groups of 1,000 and NIH RePORTER describes "4,000+ people"; the tier-1 figure of 4,000 is used. Version scope: the v3.0.0 documentation "About" page states that it is associated with a version "which contains data from the participants of the pilot study phase", identical wording to the v2.0.0 page, which conflicts with the tier-1 FAIRhub metadata recording 2,280 participants collected from 19 July 2023 to 1 May 2025; the tier-1 statement is used. Both the healthsheet and the RO-Crate describe version 3.0.0 as covering data "up through the end of the second year of the study", while the changelog table in the README attributes 863 participants to year 2 and 1,213 to year 3; the date range 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 is consistent across sources and is used. Sampling: the healthsheet's "all possible instances" answer conflicts with the registered "Non-Probability Sample" sampling method and the documented wave-based recruitment; the conflict and its resolution are recorded on the sampling_strategies entry. Size arithmetic: summing the nine datatype directory sizes reported in the dataset structure description gives 3,815,969,360,064 bytes, which is 419,614 bytes less than the stated total of 3,815,969,779,678 bytes; this record states the total as published and notes the difference, which is plausibly attributable to the root-level metadata files but is not accounted for by any source. Summing the nine directory file counts gives 356,334 files, exactly 9 fewer than the stated total of 356,343, matching the nine root-level metadata files enumerated in the same document. NIH RePORTER project identifiers: two project-detail records for core project OT2OD032644 appear in the bundle (10885481 in the funding reference and healthsheet, 10471118 in the README acknowledgment and the tier-4 NIH RePORTER page); the divergence is recorded on the grant entry. The protocol publication states that "T2DM and pre-diabetes are identified by screening electronic health records for ICD-10 diagnosis codes R73.09 and E11.X, respectively"; the code-to-condition mapping implied by "respectively" is reproduced here only as the pair of codes used, without asserting which code identifies which condition. Blood volume is reported as 53 mL in the protocol publication and as approximately 50-60 mL in the IRB protocol; neither figure is carried in this record because biospecimen collection is not part of the dataset.

data.name: CHoRUS Dataset
data.title: Bridge2AI: Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI
data.description: CHoRUS is a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access critical care dataset produced by the Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI project, one of four data generation projects in the NIH-funded Bridge2AI consortium. Data are collected retrospectively from the clinical systems of 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration spanning 20 academic centers, and are harmonized to unified standards: structured electronic health record data are standardized to the OMOP Common Data Model, imaging from PACS is held as DICOM, bedside monitor telemetry as WFDB waveforms, hospital EEG as EDF+ and Persyst, and clinical notes are extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit. The current released dataset reported by the project website comprises 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU settings, 1.6 billion rows of EHR OMOP data, 7,642 admissions with radiology data, and 23 Tb of waveform data; the anticipated final dataset covers 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities. All data types are under controlled access. As presented in September 2025, OMOP and telemetry data reside in a cloud enclave, clinical notes are stored locally at the contributing sites except for tokens, imaging de-identification was in process for a larger cohort, and EEG extraction was in process. Data acquisition, standardization and modality expansion continue within the NIH project period 2022-09-01 through 2026-11-30.
data.source_caveats: The two mid-tier sources report different admission totals for the released data: the project website (project_documentation, higher ranked) states a Current Released Dataset of 50,000 patient admissions, while the September 2025 AIM-AHEAD informational webinar (cohort_2_webinar) states that "As of August 2025" the dataset "covers 14 different hospitals with over 45K unique admissions"; the higher-ranked website figure is used here and the webinar figure is recorded in this caveat. Imaging volume is likewise reported two ways and on different units: the website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data, the webinar reports 1000 images currently available with de-identification in process for a larger cohort. Anticipated final figures (100,000 admissions, 9 modalities) are stated by the website as anticipated, not released. The webinar's data-type table has a Metadata column containing both "Yes" and "Planned" values and a separate column naming per-modality metadata schemas, but the table's text is interleaved in the bundle in a way that does not permit reliable assignment of those column values to individual data types, so neither per-modality metadata status nor per-modality metadata schema is asserted here; only the table's unambiguous Data standard column is used. The project website carries a site-wide banner reading "This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives" (spelling as published). The chorus-ai GitHub overview was captured 2025-11-14 and is the lowest-ranked source in the bundle.
data.conforms_to: OMOP Common Data Model for structured EHR data (demographics, medication administration, procedures, diagnoses and nursing flowsheets); DICOM for imaging; WFDB for waveform telemetry; EDF+ and Persyst for waveform EEG; OHNLP for extracted and tokenized clinical notes.
data.was_derived_from: Routine clinical documentation and device data from the electronic health record, PACS imaging archives, bedside monitor gateway/middleware, and hospital EEG databases of 14 contributing hospitals.

purposes.response: To develop a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset while ensuring the methods promote privacy, accountability and clinical benefit, and while promoting a new generation of AI clinicians and scientists.
To develop the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set to answer the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
To create ethically sourced datasets and tools around artificial intelligence and to create best practices for AI in health, in collaboration with the other Bridge2AI data generation projects.

To develop capabilities across a multi-center network to acquire, standardize, tokenize, store, visualize and label structured EHR data, tokenized unstructured EHR data, telemetry and EEG waveforms, imaging, and social determinants of health.
To ensure that data elements feature appropriate contextual factors such as geographic distance to the nearest hospital.

tasks.response: Characterizing acute and critical care illness.
Predicting complications among patients with acute or critical illness.
Measuring treatment response among patients with acute or critical illness.
External validation of AI/ML models against a sequestered holdout dataset, to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models for implementation in acute and critical care.

addressing_gaps.response: There is an urgent need for infrastructure to support artificial intelligence and machine learning in critical care; developing high-resolution multi-center data sets is a critical first step towards actionable and trustworthy AI.
Existing resources lack a diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready dataset for the grand challenge of improving recovery from acute illness.
Absence of sequestered holdout data for external validation of models developed on critical care data, which the project addresses by sequestering holdout datasets.
Lack of unified standards across multi-modal EHR, waveform, imaging and text data, which the project addresses through harmonization and validated semantic mappings.

acquisition_methods.acquisition_details: Retrospective data collection: data documented during routine clinical care are extracted from the source systems of contributing hospitals (EHR, PACS, bedside monitors and gateway or middleware, and the hospital EEG database) and delivered as site data extracts.
Derived content: unstructured EHR text is extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit, and OMOP Location entities are geocoded with open source code via DeGauss.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Bedside monitors with gateway/middleware capture for waveform telemetry, converted with the CHoRUS waveform conversion scripts maintained in the chorus_waveform repository.
The OHNLP toolkit, used to extract and tokenize clinical notes at contributing sites.
Site data extracts created and uploaded using the chorus-extract-upload tooling, following standard operating protocols published on the centralized Chorus_SOP documentation site.

collection_timeframes.timeframe_details: Retrospective collection of previously recorded clinical data at contributing hospitals; as presented in September 2025, the assembled dataset reflected a state as of August 2025, with further acquisition continuing within the project period.

direct_collection.collection_details: Data are not collected from individuals for the purpose of this dataset; they are retrospectively extracted from clinical source systems at contributing hospitals and delivered to the CHoRUS environment as site data extracts.

sampling_strategies.strategies: Sampling to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies; federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort across the contributing centers.
sampling_strategies.source_caveats: The bundle states the sampling intent but does not describe the executed sampling frame, inclusion criteria, or any verification of representativeness.

raw_data_sources.raw_data_format: Source EHR formats, transformed to the OMOP Common Data Model (demographics, medication administration with dosing time-stamped upon each infusion change or dose administration, procedures documented by providers, diagnoses documented by providers, and high-frequency nursing flowsheet documentation).

raw_data_sources.raw_data_format: Free text, extracted and tokenized using the OHNLP toolkit.

preprocessing_strategies.preprocessing_details: Standardization of source clinical data to the OMOP Common Data Model, supported by validated semantic mappings for connecting clinical data in various source formats to international standards; pooled tabular mappings and an associated clinical validation SOP are maintained in the chorus-mapping repository.
Extraction and tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text using the OHNLP toolkit, so that only tokens leave the contributing site.
Transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification; imaging de-identification was in process for the larger cohort as of September 2025.
Waveform conversion using the documentation and conversion scripts maintained in the chorus_waveform repository, with additional resources supporting the preparation and release of waveforms.
Geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, using open source code maintained in the UF-Geocoding repository.

cleaning_strategies.cleaning_details: Characterization reports are produced and returned to contributing sites following their data submissions, allowing sites to identify and resolve issues in their extracts.

Standard operating protocols instruct data contributing sites on best practices for curating and delivering interoperable datasets; SOP documents undergo an internal validation and review process before publication.

splits.split_details: The project states that the dataset will also provision a holdout test set, accessible for model external validation to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models; sequestering holdout datasets for external validation is described as a planned project activity rather than a released partition.

known_limitations.limitation_description: Imaging coverage is partial: as of the September 2025 webinar only 1000 images were available, with de-identification in process for a larger cohort.
EEG waveform data were still being extracted at the time of the September 2025 webinar and were therefore not fully available to users.
Clinical note text is stored locally at the contributing sites rather than in the enclave; only tokens are centrally available, which constrains analyses requiring full note text.
The dataset covers acute and critical care admissions (ICU, PICU and NICU) contributed by 14 hospitals, so it does not represent care outside these settings or these institutions.
The released dataset of 50,000 admissions is smaller than the anticipated final dataset of 100,000 admissions across 9 data modalities.

known_biases.bias_description: The cohort is assembled from 14 data contributing hospitals within a collaboration of 20 academic centers, so patient case mix reflects the populations served by those centers.
known_biases.mitigation_strategy: Federated access is intended to enable sampling methods that ensure a balanced and diverse cohort; the project additionally samples to ensure comprehensive sets of patient conditions and clinical treatment strategies, and patient-focused efforts determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.
known_biases.source_caveats: The bundle documents the project's bias-management intent and the composition of the contributing network; it does not report a measured bias assessment for the released data.

sensitive_elements.sensitivity_details: The dataset consists of clinical data about critically ill patients, including diagnoses, procedures, medication administration, nursing flowsheets, clinical notes, imaging, telemetry and EEG waveforms, and social determinants of health with geographic context such as distance to the nearest hospital.

confidential_elements.confidentiality_details: Every data type is listed with controlled access. OMOP and telemetry data sit in the enclave; clinical notes are not placed in the enclave but stored locally at contributing sites, with only tokens shared.

is_deidentified.method: Extraction and tokenization of unstructured EHR text with the OHNLP toolkit; de-identification of imaging, in process for the larger cohort as of September 2025; transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification.
is_deidentified.deidentification_details: De-identification is combined with controlled access rather than relied on alone: users are granted access to a provisioned environment after registration and a signed licensing agreement. Identifiable source material remains at the contributing sites, where clinical note text is stored locally and only tokens are shared.

participant_privacy.anonymization_method: Tokenization of clinical note text, imaging de-identification, and transformations designed to limit re-identification.
participant_privacy.privacy_techniques: A privacy scan tool for medical records is maintained by the project, alongside controlled access to all data types.
participant_privacy.reidentification_risk: The project describes transforming data using approaches that limit re-identification, and patient-focused efforts to determine ethical and legal approaches to manage privacy.

special_populations: Includes pediatric (PICU) and neonatal (NICU) intensive care admissions as well as adult critically ill patients.
human_subject_research.notes: The dataset is assembled retrospectively from the clinical records of critically ill patients, with a target of more than 100,000 critically ill patients across the project.

special_protections: All data types are under controlled access; clinical notes remain at the contributing sites except for tokens, and data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification.
at_risk_populations.notes: Pediatric and neonatal intensive care admissions are within scope, and the population consists of acutely and critically ill patients.

ethical_reviews.review_details: The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing, and evaluates community perspectives on clinical care AI to find ways to increase trustworthiness of provenance and privacy in AI.
ethical_reviews.source_caveats: The bundle documents these ethics activities as project workstreams (the CHoRUS Ethics pillar, "Ethical and Trustworthy AI"); it names no institutional review board, ethics committee or compliance certification, and no reviewing organization is asserted here.

maintainers.maintainer_details: The CHoRUS GitHub organization hosts 28 repositories of software, semantic mappings, SOPs and project management overviews; a package status page lists versions, maintainers and other metadata about CHoRUS packages, and a web guide for contributors and users is compiled in the chorus-developer repository.

updates.update_details: The dataset is growing toward an anticipated final dataset of 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. As of the September 2025 webinar, imaging de-identification was in process for a larger cohort and EEG extraction was in process; contributing sites provide regular status updates on their extract progress, tracked on the Standards and Data Acquisition project boards.

extension_mechanism.extension_details: Contributing sites follow the interactive workflow diagram and SOP documents on the Chorus_SOP site to create and submit data extracts, and post issues to the Standards or Data Acquisition discussion areas. Clinical collaborators contribute to semantic mapping through the chorus-mapping repository, which holds documentation, pooled tabular mappings and a clinical validation SOP. Software contributors work through the repositories of the chorus-ai organization.

examples: The datasets are being used for training activities and publications.

Building machine-learning and AI-derived models that characterize acute and critical care illness, predict complications, and measure treatment response, in order to improve the care and outcomes of patients requiring critical care.
Validating externally developed models against a sequestered holdout dataset, an activity the project plans in order to aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models.
Hands-on AI/ML training in the CHoRUS ecosystem, including structured EHR datasets, clinical deep learning, ethics of clinical AI, and the OHDSI/OMOP common data model.

The AIM-AHEAD Bridge2AI for Clinical Care Training Program announced Cohort 2 in a September 2025 informational webinar: up to 30 trainees were to be selected, with notice of award on 10 November 2025 and the program running from 17 November 2025 to 31 July 2026, and would receive hands-on training on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Network, leveraging the CHoRUS data and tools to create practical use cases and conduct collaborative research on the Bridge2AI Clinical Care Cloud platform.
intended_uses.usage_notes: As of the source webinar (9 September 2025), the Cohort 2 application deadline had not passed and no trainees had been selected; this is an announced program rather than a use in progress.

other_tasks.task_details: Beyond model development, the data serve as a teaching corpus: canonical Jupyter notebooks, workshops on the OHDSI tool stack and the OHDSI/OMOP common data model, and didactics on generative AI and specific use cases are delivered on the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud.

future_use_impacts.impact_details: The project anticipates that the dataset will catalyze biomedical research and expertise needed to promote patient-focused deployment of AI in acute and critical care, and that the holdout set will aid marketplace adoption of AI-developed models.

Because the data derive from critically ill patients, the project pairs future use with privacy safeguards: transformations that limit re-identification, community-facing ethics focus groups on what data is appropriate for public sharing, and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape to manage privacy and bias while accounting for social determinants of health.

data.title: Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)
data.description: The June 2026 Data Release of Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge in the NIH Bridge2AI program. CM4AI generates multi-modal data including protein-protein interaction (PPI), spatial localization, and genetic perturbation data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat treatment) and induced pluripotent stem cells (with and without differentiation). This Beta release includes perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and iPSC-derived neuron progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with treatment; and immunofluorescence images in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment. The overarching objective of CM4AI is to deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under treated and untreated conditions.

The CM4AI project web pages (tier 2) report cumulative project-level counts (1,374 protein interactions; 53,788 immunofluorescent images; 7,023 total proteins investigated; 11,739 genes targeted; 21.4 TB data volume) that are attributed to the CM4AI project as a whole rather than to this single release, and are therefore not asserted as release-level totals here. The bundle contains a Nature publication (tier 3) describing a U2OS cell map produced by the same investigators and pipeline; that is a distinct dataset and is recorded under related_datasets. The conforms_to value is carried from the tier-3 preprint and the tier-5 March 2025 and June 2025 releases rather than from the June 2026 release page itself. The June 2026 release page carries a Dataset Description block dated (2025-06-30) although the release itself was published 2026-06-17; the release page also gives a Data Creation Date of 2025-02-27, which is reused verbatim from earlier releases in this Dataverse collection. Creator names are rendered as the bundle states them, which for several authors is surname plus initial only.

purposes.response: To map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning.

To deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under treated and untreated conditions.
To produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, in order to enable transformative biomedical AI research.

To broadly stimulate research and development in "visible" machine learning systems informed by multi-scale cell and tissue architecture, which are not black boxes but are built directly on knowledge maps of cell and tissue architecture.

addressing_gaps.response: In genomics and precision medicine, machine learning models are often "black boxes," predicting phenotypes from genotypes without understanding the mechanisms by which such translation occurs. This project addresses that deficiency by creating a library of large-scale maps of cellular structure and function across demographic and disease contexts.

Cell maps provide a foundation for downstream applications in human genomics, including interpretation of genetic variants and mutations, which existing black-box models do not support; CM4AI addresses this by producing AI-ready hierarchical maps of cell architecture from multimodal interrogation of disease-relevant cell lines.

tasks.response: Construction of hierarchical cell maps: directed acyclic graphs in which each node represents an assembly of proteins in proximity at a given scale, spanning from large assemblies representing cell compartments to small assemblies of proteins in close proximity.
Self-supervised multimodal embedding of protein-protein interaction and immunofluorescence image features into a shared low-dimensional space.
Multi-resolution community detection over protein-protein similarities to generate a hierarchy of protein assemblies.
Development of visible machine learning models (visible neural networks) that interrogate how protein assemblies in the cell affect cell-level phenotype predictions.
Interpretation of genetic variants and mutations in human genomics using cell maps as a structural prior.

acquisition_methods.acquisition_details: Protein-protein interaction data acquired by affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) on endogenously tagged cell lines and by size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS) for proteome-wide complex and interaction mapping, used as two orthogonal mass spectrometry-based approaches.

Spatial proteomics acquired by immunofluorescence (IF) subcellular microscopy, using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols on a pipetting robot for the MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines.

Genetic perturbation data acquired by single-cell CRISPR (CRISPRi) perturbation screens by cell type, using a CRISPR lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene, in cell lines expressing inducible dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) on endogenously tagged cell lines.
Size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS) for proteome-wide complex and interaction mapping.

Immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) and confocal microscopy, with four color channels: DAPI for nuclei (blue), calreticulin antibody for endoplasmic reticulum (yellow), tubulin antibody for microtubules (red), and antibody against the protein of interest (green).
Single-cell CRISPR screens using a CRISPR lentiviral library with 6 guide RNAs per gene in cell lines expressing inducible dCas9, sequenced with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.
