data.notes: CM4AI consists of three pillars - Data, People, and Ethics - organized into six modules: Data Acquisition, Tools, and Standards (Data); Skills and Workforce Development, and Teaming (People); and Ethics. The project defines AI-Ready biomedical data as fully characterized FAIR data of known provenance that can be ethically and reliably processed by AI applications, whose models and software are available and well-described for validation and re-use, and whose predictions may be fully explained and interpreted to the user as needed; the project's stated criteria are FAIR, Provenanced, Characterized, Explainable, and Ethical. The Standards Module's FAIRSCAPE framework assigns persistent, resolvable, globally unique identifiers using the ARK scheme, with provenance entailments expressed in the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology. The CM4AI Tools Module maintains the Multi-Scale Integrated Cell (MuSIC) pipeline, which integrates protein-protein interaction and immunofluorescence image data by node2vec and Human Protein Atlas deep learning embeddings, contrastive co-embedding, and multi-resolution community detection, and which annotates resulting assemblies by alignment to Gene Ontology and Reactome and by a large language model naming approach; this pipeline produces the computed cell maps that the June 2026 release states are not included in this release.

data.description: Bridge2AI-Voice is an ethically sourced, multi-site dataset of voice, speech, breathing and cough data linked to demographic, clinical and validated-questionnaire information, built to support research into voice as a biomarker of health. Version 3.1.0 covers 833 adult participants recruited at five North American sites and selected for conditions that manifest within the voice waveform: voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders and respiratory disorders, alongside control participants. Participants completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks on a tablet application, with a headset where possible, together with demographic, confounder, disease-specific and validated-questionnaire instruments; clinical diagnoses were validated by clinicians against site gold standards. The public release distributes data considered low risk — spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, pitch and periodicity traces, Speech Articulatory Coding articulatory estimates, phonetic posteriorgrams, openSMILE, Praat and parselmouth static features, per-recording audio quality metrics, per-recording metadata and phenotype tables — rather than the original waveforms. Raw audio is disseminated separately, under controlled access only.
data.was_derived_from: Raw audio recordings of standardized acoustic tasks captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application, together with questionnaire and clinical data captured in REDCap, collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol.
data.citation: Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., Powell, M., Dorr, D., Payne, P., Ravitsky, V., Bélisle-Pipon, J., Bahr, R., Watts, S., Bolser, D., Siu, J., Lerner-Ellis, J., Rudzicz, F., Boyer, M., Abdel-Aty, Y., Ahmed Syed, T., Anibal, J., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66
data.source_caveats: This record describes the adult Bridge2AI-Voice dataset at PhysioNet version 3.1.0, published 2026-05-01, which is the most recent version present in the source bundle; the Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset is recorded as a related dataset rather than as part of this one. The project documentation at docs.b2ai-voice.org answers several healthsheet questions against earlier releases — it reports "version 3.0 containing ~61,937 voice-derived recordings from 833 adult participants", heads its de-identification section "Methods of De-identification for v3.0.0", and elsewhere refers to "The current v.2.0.0 dataset"; where that documentation and the PhysioNet 3.1.0 record differ, the higher-ranked PhysioNet record has been preferred here. The documentation also gives distribution and maintenance answers for the Health Data Nexus platform, where version 1.0 was published, while versions 1.1 onward are published on PhysioNet. The documentation's data pre-processing section states that "The raw audio files and the questionnaire data retrieved from ReproSchema-UI or exported from REDCap were converted to be compliant with the Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0" and shows a b2ai-voice-audio layout of dataset_description.json, phenotype and sub-<id>/ses-<id>/audio directories; the PhysioNet 3.1.0 release described here has a features, metadata and phenotype layout and does not state conformance to any data standard, so no standard is asserted for this release. Email addresses in the scraped documentation are redacted as "[email protected]", so only the DACO@b2ai-voice.org address that appears verbatim in the PhysioNet notices is recorded. The award identifier is written variously across sources: the PhysioNet acknowledgement gives "3OT2OD032720-01S1", NIH RePORTER gives application "3OT2OD032720-01S3" under core project "OT2OD032720", and the documentation footer gives "Award #3Tf-OTOD03272001S2" and "3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1", both apparently corrupted in transcription. The 2025 feasibility publication in the bundle reports a separate 47-participant study of the collection application under USF IRB 004890 and its participant characteristics, task metrics and limitations are not attributed to this dataset.

purposes.response: To create an ethically sourced flagship dataset that enables future research in artificial intelligence and supports critical insights into the use of voice as a biomarker of health.

To generate a large multi-institutional, ethically sourced and diverse voice dataset linked to multimodal health biomarkers in order to fuel voice AI research and promote integration of voice as a biomarker of health in clinical care.

To enable the development, benchmarking or validation of clinically applicable machine-learning models for diagnosing a wide range of health conditions using voice data, including vocal pathologies and neurological, psychiatric, respiratory and pediatric voice disorders.

addressing_gaps.response: The absence of large-scale, diverse and well-documented voice data for clinical machine-learning applications. Previous studies of machine learning-based voice diagnosis produced promising results, but their sample sizes were too small or they lacked the key metadata needed for training robust, clinically useful models.
The absence of standards for how voice and speech data are collected, which makes comparing studies and pooling data across them difficult.
The confinement of existing work to small- to medium-sized datasets with limited data outside acoustic measures and no linkage to multi-modal health data.

tasks.response: Training machine-learning models for disease detection and classification using voice data, with labels drawn from diagnostic categories including vocal pathologies, neurological disorders, psychiatric conditions and respiratory disorders.
Screening, diagnosis and monitoring of health conditions through voice biomarkers.

other_tasks.task_details: Cohort selection: the questionnaire-derived phenotype tables distributed in the phenotype folder can be used to select cohorts for downstream analysis.

intended_uses.usage_notes: The dataset is primarily intended for research applications, specifically the development of AI and machine-learning models for healthcare, and it supports clinical research in disease screening, diagnosis and monitoring through voice biomarkers.
Under the Registered Access Agreement the dataset is intended solely for commercial and non-commercial research purposes by Authorized Researchers.

discouraged_uses.discouragement_details: Non-clinical and non-research applications such as hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments, or any form of surveillance that could lead to discrimination or harm. These limitations are intended to prevent unethical or biased outcomes that could negatively impact individuals based on their health conditions or voice characteristics.

prohibited_uses.prohibition_reason: Re-identification attempts are barred because the Registered Data Access Agreement reflects the consortium's commitment to advancing ethical and trustworthy research practices that respect and protect the rights and interests of research participants.
prohibited_uses.notes: The dataset is not to be used to attempt to re-identify research participants, nor for any actions that could reasonably lead to re-identification.

prohibited_uses.prohibition_reason: Uses that could foreseeably cause harm or stigmatization to research participants, their families, communities or specific populations are barred in order to protect the rights and interests of those participants and populations.

Intellectual property protections, database rights or related rights may not be used in a manner that restricts or limits access to any part of the dataset or to any conclusions derived from it, so that future use of the dataset remains unrestricted in alignment with the Open Science principles upheld by the consortium.

data_collectors.collector_details: Research teams, which may include medical, graduate or undergraduate students, coordinated with clinicians and doctors to identify appropriate participants, and data was collected in the clinic with the assistance of a trained research assistant.

Clinicians and doctors listed under the IRB as co-investigators identified eligible participants and provided the clinical diagnoses used as gold standard labels; they were added to the consortium so that their names are included on consortium-level publications.
Hospital staff were not involved in scheduling but assisted in the logistics of coordinating data collection.

acquisition_methods.acquisition_details: Acoustic tasks were recorded and questionnaires administered during a standardized collection session; diagnoses were confirmed by clinicians reviewing audio and/or imaging data, electronic health records, or medication prescriptions.

The released acoustic features are computed from the collected audio rather than observed directly: spectral, articulatory, phonetic and prosodic representations are derived from the standardized waveform by software.

collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: A custom Bridge2AI-Voice application running on a tablet, with a head-mounted headset and microphone used for recording when possible. Collection hardware comprised iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; distinct iPad devices were used at each site.
REDCap, which held the questionnaire instruments and from which the collected data was exported and converted using an open source library developed by the project team.

collection_timeframes.timeframe_details: The project documentation records that the data was collected over a period of 12 months.
collection_timeframes.source_caveats: Neither the documentation nor the PhysioNet release states start and end dates for collection, and the 12-month figure is given in a healthsheet written against an earlier release, so it may not cover the whole of the collection behind version 3.1.0.

direct_collection.collection_details: Data was collected directly from the individuals concerned during a clinic session rather than obtained via third parties such as hospitals or app companies.

sampling_strategies.strategies: Non-probability sampling. Recruitment of participants at high volume expert clinics within participating academic institutions, screened against per-diagnosis inclusion and exclusion criteria before the clinic visit.
sampling_strategies.source_data: Patients presenting at specialty clinics and institutions in five predetermined cohort groups, plus participants without the conditions of interest serving as controls.
sampling_strategies.why_not_representative: The dataset is a sample of a larger, ongoing collection and is not representative because it was collected at a limited number of geographic locations.
representative_verification: No verification of representativeness is reported; the project states an intention to make the sample more representative by shifting to remote collection and by designing recruitment to control for more variables.

instances.label_description: Diagnostic labels are the result of a clinical assessment of the participant. At each site a local clinician provided the diagnosis based on a clinical interview and appropriate work-up; for the psychiatric disorders cohort the assessment was determined from the participant's electronic health record or an active prescription, made outside data collection by an appropriately licensed clinician.

missing: Responses to optional questionnaire items and to cohort-specific instruments
why_missing: Some questions are optional, and each individual answered a common set of questions and then responded to additional questions relevant to their primary diagnostic category.
There may be data collection irregularities that caused some information to be missing from individual instances.

instances.instance_type: audio recording, represented by its derived features
instances.notes: Per-feature record counts in the version 3.1.0 release are: torchaudio pitch 32,522; sparc periodicity and sparc pitch 31,872 each; sparc loudness 31,855; phonetic posteriorgrams 29,289; spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC 29,278 each; sparc EMA 28,640. Counts differ between features because representations derived from sensitive records and audio checks were withheld, and because some files could not generate certain features. The release does not state a single recording total and none is computed here.

relationships.relationship_details: Relationships between individual participants are not made explicit; the participants are unrelated to one another.

Within a participant, recordings are grouped into sessions. Most participants completed collection in a single session, but a subset required multiple sessions, so there may be more than one session per participant and more than one row per participant in the phenotype files; a participant is not required to give the same response at each visit.

splits.split_details: No recommended train, validation or test splits are predefined. Researchers are encouraged to create their own data splits based on their specific requirements.

subpopulations.identification: Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, and participants are assigned to disease cohort categories — voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders — or to the control group.
subpopulations.distribution: The public data releases do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories, and the dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors.

variables.description: Unique identifier for the participant, carried by every feature file and phenotype table.
Unique identifier for the recording session; a participant may contribute more than one session.
The acoustic task performed in the recording from which the feature was derived.
The number of time frames associated with the feature tensor for that recording.

raw_data_sources.source_description: Raw audio recordings of the acoustic tasks, captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice application on a tablet with a headset microphone.
raw_data_sources.access_details: Not included in the PhysioNet release. Retained but not publicly accessible; disseminated through controlled access only, via Synapse at https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/, with requests directed to the access committee at DACO@b2ai-voice.org.

raw_data_sources.source_description: Questionnaire, demographic, confounder and diagnostic data captured through the collection application and held in REDCap.
raw_data_sources.access_details: Exported and converted with the project's open source b2aiprep library into the released phenotype tables.

preprocessing_strategies.preprocessing_details: Raw audio was standardized by converting to monaural and resampling to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing filter applied.

Spectrograms were computed from the standardized audio using the short-time Fast Fourier Transform with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT, then downsampled by a factor of two in the time domain. Mel spectrograms use the same parameters with 60 Mel bins, and 60 Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients were extracted from the spectrograms.

Articulatory features were generated with the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package, giving kinematic traces of vocal tract articulators and source features together with measures of loudness, periodicity and pitch, all gathered at 50 Hz.
Phonetic posteriorgrams, a time-varying categorical distribution over acoustic units of speech at 100 Hz across 40 phoneme categories, were generated with the ppgs package.
Acoustic features were extracted with openSMILE, and phonetic and prosodic features — measures of fundamental frequency, formants and voice quality — were computed with Parselmouth and Praat.
Transcriptions were generated using OpenAI's Whisper Large model.

cleaning_strategies.cleaning_details: An audit protocol was applied: generate missingness tables; check distributions and outliers; check categorical responses against the schema; run quality control metrics for audio tasks; and for waveforms check the amount of silence and the duration, and for speech check the produced speech relative to the intended passage. All processing was performed with the b2aiprep and SenseLab toolkits.
Audio quality control metrics derived from the raw recordings are released alongside the features as audio_quality_metrics.tsv, one row per audio recording.

labeling_strategies.labeling_details: Gold standard diagnostic labels were taken from clinical assessment. At each site a local clinician provided the diagnosis; for the psychiatric disorders cohort the label was determined from the participant's electronic health record or an active prescription.
annotator_demographics: Typically the clinician at the site of data collection, or a clinician external to it where a prior diagnostic assessment was used.
labeling_strategies.data_annotation_protocol: Per Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10 codes.
labeling_strategies.data_annotation_platform: The collection application and REDCap, with clinical validation recorded in the diagnosis instruments.
labeling_strategies.notes: Human-level performance on the applications the dataset is meant to address is reported to vary widely.

machine_annotation_tools.tool_descriptions: Whisper Large generated the transcriptions. openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth and torchaudio generated the static acoustic, phonetic and prosodic features and the time-varying spectral representations. sparc generated articulatory estimates and source measures; ppgs generated phonetic posteriorgrams. b2aiprep organized and preprocessed the dataset and merged the source data into the phenotype files; SenseLab processed the audio files for research tasks.
tool_accuracy: Certain aspects of the data, for example transcription, were generated using off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness.

missing_data_documentation.missing_data_patterns: Phenotype data files contain a row for a participant only if at least one column is not missing, and each participant answered a common set of questions plus additional questions relevant to their primary diagnostic category. Feature files omit recordings for which a given feature could not be generated, whether because of length or other issues.
missing_data_documentation.missing_data_causes: Optional questionnaire items, data collection irregularities, cohort-specific branching of the instruments, and removal of representations derived from sensitive records and audio checks.
missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy: The dataset was audited internally for missingness and consistency by the data release team, and a missingness table is included with the dataset.

anomalies.anomaly_details: Different sites have different collection configurations, and the collection protocol changed over the course of the study.
Noise artifacts, variations in diagnostic practices, inaccurate questionnaire responses and underreporting are possible confounding factors in the collected data.

Recordings were made with a head-mounted headset and microphone that could be at slightly different distances between sessions, and the clinical diagnosis, depending on the disorder, was performed by one clinician or based on an electronic health record or prescription.

known_biases.bias_description: Participants were recruited at a small number of high volume expert clinics; groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or who are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited.
known_biases.mitigation_strategy: The project states an intention to shift toward remote collection and to design recruitment so that more variables are controlled.

known_biases.bias_description: The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors, and the public releases do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories.
known_biases.mitigation_strategy: Users should consider the multivariate distribution when assessing utility for different questions.

known_biases.bias_description: Participants were screened for different disorders based on site, so participants with different labels also had their data collected on different devices, confounding label with recording apparatus and site.
affected_subsets: All disease cohorts, since cohorts were recruited at different sites with distinct iPad devices.

known_limitations.limitation_description: The dataset is a non-probability sample of a larger, ongoing collection and is not representative, having been collected at a limited number of geographic locations.
known_limitations.scope_impact: Limits the generalization of models derived from the dataset to other populations and settings.

known_limitations.limitation_description: Communication with participants and the collection instruments were in English, and eligibility required the ability to read and speak English; Spanish versions of the protocol are described as under development.
known_limitations.recommended_mitigation: Treat findings as specific to English-speaking participants until non-English collection is released.

known_limitations.limitation_description: The public release contains data considered low risk — derivations such as spectrograms and other features — and not the original voice recordings, which are available only through a separate controlled access process.
Changes in diagnostic criteria or practices over the collection period could be a source of distribution shift.

The multimodal data described in the collection protocol — laryngoscopy and other imaging, genomic sequencing, spirometry and other measures extracted from electronic health records — is not part of this release, which distributes audio-derived features, per-recording metadata and phenotype tables only.
known_limitations.source_caveats: The project documentation states explicitly of the preceding release that "no external data is released in this v3.0.0 release"; the version 3.1.0 data description likewise lists only features, metadata and phenotype content.

warnings: Free speech tasks: where transcriptions of free speech are present, offensive, insulting or threatening content cannot be completely avoided, since research participants are responsible for their choice of language.
Questionnaire content covering mental health, traumatic life experiences and other distressing subject matter is collected in the mood and psychiatric cohort instruments.
content_warnings.source_caveats: The warning about free speech transcriptions is the project documentation's healthsheet answer. In the PhysioNet releases, transcripts of free speech audio were removed from version 1.1 and spectrograms and similar features were excluded where the audio contained free speech, so the exposure in version 3.1.0 is narrower than the documentation's answer implies.

sensitive_elements.sensitivity_details: The dataset includes race and ethnicity information and sexual orientation information.
The dataset includes socioeconomic and health information, including clinical diagnoses across voice, neurological, psychiatric and respiratory conditions.

Voice itself is a biometric characteristic capable of identifying the speaker, which is why all raw voice data was removed from the registered access release and is disseminated only under controlled access.

confidential_elements.confidentiality_details: The project documentation records that the dataset does not contain data considered confidential in the sense of legal privilege, doctor-patient confidentiality, or the content of individuals' non-public communications.

is_deidentified.method: HIPAA Safe Harbor, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers and of non-identifying but highly sensitive fields, and by withholding of all raw audio.
is_deidentified.identifiers_removed: HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers, including names, geographic locators, date information at a resolution finer than years, phone and fax numbers, email addresses, IP addresses, Social Security numbers, medical record numbers, health plan beneficiary numbers, device identifiers, license numbers, account numbers, vehicle identifiers, website URLs, full face photos, biometric identifiers and any unique identifiers; state and province, with country of data collection retained; select geographic or demographic identifiers and some information about household composition or cultural identity; and non-identifying but highly sensitive elements such as household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences.
is_deidentified.deidentification_details: All raw voice data was removed because it has the potential to cause individual re-identification or to be used for illicit or unauthorized purposes, and only extracted features are released. Raw audio transcripts were reviewed and any recordings containing potentially identifying information or external voices were removed from the release; spectrograms and similar features were excluded where the audio contained free speech, while static and other features that do not encode the sensitive information were retained. Sensitive fields flagged in the REDCap data dictionary were removed. K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved.

participant_privacy.anonymization_method: Removal of direct identifiers, removal of indirect identifiers where their combination with other public data created a significant risk of re-identification, and release of features extracted from the audio in place of the audio itself.
participant_privacy.privacy_techniques: Withholding of all raw voice recordings from the registered access release; Review and removal of recordings containing potentially identifying information or external voices; Removal of transcripts and derived representations of free speech; Removal of fields encoded as sensitive in the REDCap data dictionary.
participant_privacy.reidentification_risk: Voice is unique to the speaker and cannot be fully de-identified, so raw audio is disseminated only through controlled access to authorized researchers; K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved for the released tables. Recipients of the raw data are contractually barred from using it, alone or with any other information, to attempt to contact the individuals who are its subjects.
participant_privacy.data_linkage: Records are linked across sessions and across feature and phenotype files by a study participant identifier; consenting participants also permitted investigators to access medical information through electronic health record platforms in order to perform gold standard validation of diagnoses and symptoms.

data_protection_impacts.impact_details: The project documentation answers directly that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted.

irb_approval: Data collection and sharing was approved by the University of South Florida Institutional Review Board. The multi-site protocol was submitted to and approved by the USF Single IRB, with subsite IRBs reviewing through the Single IRB process; the protocol provides that Canadian institutions apply separately to their own research ethics boards.
human_subject_research.ethics_review_board: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board
regulatory_compliance: HIPAA de-identification rules were applied to the released dataset. The data transferred under the Data Transfer and Use Agreement is covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality, which must be asserted against compulsory legal demands such as court orders and subpoenas for identifying information or characteristics of a research participant. The study was not conducted for a drug product or a medical device, and no data monitoring committee was appointed.
special_populations: Enrollment for the cohort released here is limited to adults, with a minimum age of 18 years and a maximum age of 120 years; pediatric participants were enrolled only through the pediatric sites and are released as a separate dataset. The protocol nonetheless lists "Obtaining Signed Assent for Children or Adults Unable to Consent" among its consent options, and the adult cohorts include participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, and mood and psychiatric diagnoses. The protocol notes that questions asked of participants in certain disease cohorts, such as mood disorders, depression and anxiety, can cause discomfort and trigger negative emotions.

ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board
ethical_reviews.review_details: Data collection and sharing for the released dataset was approved by the University of South Florida Institutional Review Board; the clinical study was submitted and approved by the USF Single IRB and by subsite IRBs through the Single IRB process. The IRB protocol records that Canadian participating institutions do not fall under the Single IRB process and apply separately to their own research ethics boards, with copies of those approvals submitted to the USF IRB.

informed_consent.consent_type: Prospective written informed consent, obtained on paper, electronically through REDCap survey forms within the application, or by video recording of the participant reading a consent statement aloud; assent was obtained where applicable for participants unable to consent.
informed_consent.consent_documentation: Paper consent documents are uploaded and saved electronically in REDCap, and all paper and electronic versions of consent are stored for a minimum of five years after completion of the study.
informed_consent.consent_scope: Research data that does not contain direct identifiers is shared with external researchers for future research through a secure database: data posing a low risk of individual re-identification is shared in registered access with the general public, and data that would pose a heightened risk if shared in full open access is shared through a controlled access mechanism with authorized researchers. The consent does not restrict use to non-commercial purposes, to a specific geographic location, to a specific type of research, to genetic research, or to research that does not involve the development of methods or algorithms.
informed_consent.withdrawal_mechanism: Participants are informed that they may withdraw from the study at any point.

collection_consents.consent_details: All participants were duly informed and agreed to the collection and use of their data via prospective informed consent, through an IRB-approved consent process conducted by research assistants in the clinic or remotely.

In clinic, potential participants were given time to consider and ask questions, were asked to explain what they had understood to the research assistant to confirm understanding, and were informed that participation is voluntary and does not affect their medical care in any way.

consent_revocations.revocation_details: Consenting participants are informed that they may withdraw from the study at any point. If a participant withdraws during or before the voice data collection, their data is not included in the database. Participants are informed that research data, including voice recordings, cannot be removed from the database once the voice data collection process is completed. Participants who withdraw may optionally complete a satisfaction survey about their reasons for withdrawal; no protected health information is collected in that survey.

collection_notifications.notification_details: Individuals were notified about the data collection: participants went through an IRB-approved consent process in which the data being collected, the methods used to secure it and the uses to which it would be put were explained.

special_protections: Enrollment for the cohort released here is limited to adults: the minimum age is 18 years and the maximum age is 120 years, and pediatric participants were enrolled only through the pediatric sites, which are released as a separate dataset.
The IRB protocol lists "Obtaining Signed Assent for Children or Adults Unable to Consent" among the consent options available under the study.

The protocol records that questions asked of participants in certain disease cohorts, such as mood disorders, depression and anxiety, can lead to possible discomfort and could trigger negative emotions for the participants.
at_risk_populations.assent_procedures: Where assent applies, the protocol provides that it be documented on a dedicated form; for young children who cannot reasonably be asked to assent due to limitations in understanding by age and development — typically children under seven years of age — assent is not sought.
at_risk_populations.source_caveats: The sources do not state whether the adult cohorts released here include participants enrolled through assent rather than personal consent, and no source characterizes this release's population as including or excluding at-risk groups, so no such determination is recorded. The adult cohorts do include participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, and with mood and psychiatric diagnoses.

participant_compensation.compensation_amount: 40 US dollars for a data collection session taking less than 90 minutes and 80 US dollars for a session taking over 90 minutes, for no more than three sessions and maximum compensation of 120 US dollars.
participant_compensation.compensation_rationale: Compensation for the participant's time; compensation was provided to the adult population only.

license_and_use_terms.license_terms: The files are released under the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License, and access requires signature of the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement. From version 3.0.0 the PhysioNet access policy is that only credentialed users who sign the data use agreement can access the files; no additional training is required. Raw audio is governed separately, requiring a Data Access Request Form, a Data Use Agreement, review by the Data Access Compliance Office and a Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at the recipient institution. Duplication as reasonably required to carry out the research project is permitted; sale of all or part of the data on any media is not. There are no fees associated with these restrictions.

restrictions: The data may be protected by copyright and other rights, including other intellectual property rights; nothing in the agreement transfers any intellectual property rights in or relating to the data to the recipient.

Recipients agree not to make intellectual property claims on the data and not to use intellectual property protection in ways that would prevent or block access to, or use of, any element of the data or conclusions drawn directly from it.

Recipients who perform further research adding intellectual and resource capital may obtain intellectual property rights on downstream discoveries, but agree to implement licensing policies that will not obstruct further research and to respect the Fort Lauderdale Agreement.
No intellectual-property-based restrictions have been imposed by third parties on the data associated with the instances.

regulatory_restrictions: No export controls apply to the dataset.
regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance: HIPAA de-identification rules were applied and direct identifiers removed. The data transferred under the Data Transfer and Use Agreement is covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality. Recipients must store the data with administrative, physical and technical safeguards adequate to protect personally identifiable information, must restrict access to authorized persons, and must report any unauthorized use or disclosure to the provider within five business days of discovery.
regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats: The Data Transfer and Use Agreement characterizes the transferred data as personally identifiable information under OMB Memorandum M-07-16 and states that it is "not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws", while the dataset documentation records that HIPAA de-identification rules were applied to the released dataset; both statements are recorded rather than reconciled.

accountable_organization.name: University of South Florida Board of Trustees
accountable_organization.description: Named as the Provider Institution in the Data Transfer and Use Agreement for the Bridge2AI Voice as a Biomarker of Health project.

data_governance.access_review_process: Access to the feature-only release is granted through registered access: users register on PhysioNet, confirm their identity under the Registered Access License, and sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement; from version 3.0.0 the applicant must be a credentialed PhysioNet user. Access to the raw audio is granted through controlled access: the applicant completes a Data Access Request Form and a Data Use Agreement, submits the application to the Data Access Compliance Office for review, and on approval has a Data Use and Transfer Agreement signed by an authorized official at their institution. The agreement takes effect only upon review and approval by the Data Access Compliance Office, which requires a distinct application. Requests for raw audio are directed to the access committee at DACO@b2ai-voice.org and the audio is served through Synapse.
stewardship_roles: Provider Institution, which supplies the data and may terminate the agreement
Provider Scientist, who signs alongside the Provider Institutional Official
Recipient Institution and Recipient Authorized Institutional Official, who bind the institution and warrant compliance
Recipient Scientist, who must retain control over the data and restrict its use to Authorized Persons named in the agreement
Data Access Compliance Office, which reviews and approves each controlled access application
data_governance.notes: The sources name an office rather than a named individual as the access contact; requests are directed to the Data Access Compliance Office mailbox, DACO@b2ai-voice.org. The project documentation additionally publishes a memorandum setting out the ethical justification for controlled access to raw voice data samples, explaining the reasoning behind this governance structure, and records that the fields treated as sensitive and removed from the release were identified by a team of ethicists.

third_party_sharing.notes: The dataset is distributed broadly to individuals outside the entity that created it, through a data publishing platform that provides publicly accessible metadata and a DOI while the dataset itself requires registered or credentialed access. Collaborators at other research organizations, and other research teams at the same organization, must apply independently for access to the raw data and sign their own Data Transfer and Use Agreement.

distribution_formats.description: Tab-delimited tables: the phenotype tables (confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaire and task), the per-recording static features, and the audio quality metrics.

JSON data dictionaries accompanying each data file and sharing its file stem, giving a description of each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type of the response.

Apache Parquet, an open-source column-oriented data file format, used for the dense binary features: phonetic posteriorgrams, the four sparc feature files, the four torchaudio feature files and the per-recording metadata file. Each element carries participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames and the feature tensor.
distribution_formats.notes: No IANA media type for Parquet is stated by the sources, so none is recorded.

distribution_dates.notes: Version 1.0 was published earlier on the Health Data Nexus platform; the documentation records that the data was published and made available at the end of November 2024.

examples: A restricted version of the dataset containing raw audio has been used in the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon.

future_use_impacts.impact_details: The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors, so users should consider the multivariate distribution when assessing utility for different questions; unexamined use could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups.

Use outside research — in hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustments or surveillance — could produce discrimination or harm on the basis of health conditions or voice characteristics, which is why such applications are excluded by the access agreement.

external_resources.source_caveats: The project documentation's healthsheet answers that the dataset "is self-contained" and gives no guarantees regarding external resources; the resources listed here are the supporting code, metadata and publications the same documentation points to.

related_datasets.notes: Version 3.0.0 of the same dataset, published 16 December 2025, which added data for 391 participants over version 2.0.1 and reorganized the phenotype files.

file_collections.name: features
file_collections.description: Audio-derived features for each recording. Dense features are distributed as Apache Parquet files, each element carrying participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames and the feature tensor; per-recording scalar features and audio quality metrics are distributed as tab-delimited files. Every data file is accompanied by a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem and describing the feature and the processing used to prepare it.

resources.name: torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet
resources.description: Spectrograms of dimension 201 by T generated with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length and a 400-point FFT; 29,278 records.

resources.name: torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet
resources.description: Mel spectrograms of dimension 60 by T generated with a 25 ms window size, 10 ms hop length, a 400-point FFT and 60 Mel bins; 29,278 records.

resources.name: torchaudio_mfcc.parquet
resources.description: Mel-frequency cepstrum coefficients of dimension 60 by T using the same parameters as the Mel spectrograms; 29,278 records.

resources.name: torchaudio_pitch.parquet
resources.description: Detected pitch (fundamental frequency) over time, dimension T, with minimum and maximum pitch of 80 and 500; 32,522 records.

resources.name: sparc_ema.parquet
resources.description: Estimated electromagnetic articulography from a deep learning model, dimension T by 12, the twelve values being X and Y positions of tongue dorsum, tongue body, tongue tip, lower incisor, upper lip and lower lip; 28,640 records.

resources.name: sparc_loudness.parquet
resources.description: Estimated loudness based on the average absolute amplitude of the waveform, dimension T, using 20 ms windows; 31,855 records.

resources.name: sparc_periodicity.parquet
resources.description: Estimated periodicity, the confidence of pitch presence, derived using 20 ms windows, dimension T; 31,872 records.

resources.name: sparc_pitch.parquet
resources.description: Estimated fundamental frequency of the audio signal over a range of 50 to 550 Hz, dimension T, computed with a different algorithm from the torchaudio pitch; 31,872 records.

resources.name: ppgs.parquet
resources.description: Phonetic posteriorgram probabilities across 40 phoneme categories, dimension 40 by T, at a frame rate of 100 Hz; 29,289 records.

resources.name: static_features.tsv
resources.description: Features derived from the raw audio with one feature per audio recording, drawn from openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth and torchaudio; one row per unique recording.

resources.name: audio_quality_metrics.tsv
resources.description: One feature per audio recording derived from the raw audio, relating to quality control metrics.

file_collections.name: phenotype
file_collections.description: Organized information collected from the participant or another individual during their encounter, as tab-delimited files each paired with a JSON data dictionary, grouped into confounders, demographics, diagnosis (per-condition files covering airway stenosis, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, anxiety, benign lesions, bipolar disorder, cognitive impairment, control, COPD and asthma, depression, glottic insufficiency, laryngeal cancer, laryngeal dystonia, laryngitis, muscle tension dysphonia, Parkinson's disease, precancerous lesions, unexplained chronic cough and unilateral vocal fold paralysis), enrollment (eligibility, enrollment form, participant), questionnaire (ADHD adult, custom affect scale, DSM-5 adult, dyspnea index, GAD-7, Leicester cough questionnaire, PANAS, PHQ-9, productive vocabulary, psychiatric history, PTSD adult, VHI-10, voice perception) and task (acoustic task, harvard sentences, random item generation, recording, session, stroop, winograd).

file_collections.name: metadata
file_collections.description: A binary Parquet file and its data dictionary holding per-recording metadata, including task instructions and prompts and information about the microphone used and its gain.

maintainers.maintainer_details: PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, hosts the release and provides continued access to credentialed researchers.
The dataset is supported by the NIH via the Bridge2AI project, under NIH Common Fund award OT2OD032720.
The Bridge2AI-Voice consortium curates the data; requests concerning access to the raw audio are handled by the access committee at DACO@b2ai-voice.org.
maintainers.source_caveats: The project documentation's maintenance answers describe hosting by the Health Data Nexus, a platform maintained by the Temerty Centre for Artificial Intelligence Research and Education in Medicine at the University of Toronto, which hosted version 1.0; versions 1.1 onward are hosted on PhysioNet.

updates.update_details: The project documentation states that further versions of the dataset will be released on a semi-annual (twice a year) basis, distributed as new versions of the dataset, with users notified through news items on the hosting platform and through standard communication channels; that statement is a plan written against the Health Data Nexus platform and an earlier release, not an observed cadence. Published versions to date are 1.0 on Health Data Nexus, then 1.1 (17 January 2025), 2.0.0 (16 April 2025), 2.0.1 (18 August 2025), 3.0.0 (16 December 2025) and 3.1.0 (1 May 2026).

version_access.version_details: Each version of the dataset has a unique DOI, and by default older versions continue to be supported, hosted and made available to researchers, though the dataset publishers reserve the right to remove access to older versions. The files for version 1.1 are no longer available from PhysioNet. Version 1.0 was published on the Health Data Nexus platform under doi:10.57764/qb6h-em84.

errata.erratum_details: Version 2.0 reprocessed the spectrograms to fix minor issues identified in the previous release and removed all spectrograms and Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients derived from free-speech files. Version 2.0.1 corrected the authorship list. Version 3.1.0 fixed broken parquet files carried over from the previous release, updated validated diagnosis information across conditions with back-filled information, rearranged some phenotypic files and renamed certain gold standard variable names.
errata.source_caveats: The project documentation states that there is no erratum and that a changelog for each dataset version is published online with the dataset metadata; the corrections recorded here are taken from those per-version release notes.

retention_limit.retention_period: Indefinite for the published dataset; two years or less for recipients of the raw data
retention_limit.retention_details: Once data is contributed, the data will be retained as long as it is useful for research purposes, possibly indefinitely. Recipients of the raw voice data under the Data Transfer and Use Agreement hold it for a shorter term: two years after the start date, upon completion of the project, upon termination, or upon expiration of the applicable ethics approval, whichever occurs first, after which the data is destroyed in accordance with the provider's instructions and a written certification of destruction is submitted within thirty days. Identifiable data and the sheets linking participant numbers to participant information are held by each collecting institution for a maximum of ten years after study completion and then destroyed.

extension_mechanism.extension_details: Others may publish a derivative dataset that references the original source, made available under the same conditions as the source data. For the code used to produce the data, the open-source repositories provide discussion forums and issue pages for public discussion of data preprocessing, and a pull request mechanism for contributing improvements to the preprocessing code.
